up-to-us.plain: Up to us: settled by your own mind alone, so that nobody can block it.
up-to-us.why: The whole book rests on this test. Epictetus asks it of every event before anything else.

opinion.plain: Your judgement of what a thing is and whether it is good or bad. Not taste.
opinion.why: For the Stoics the judgement, not the event, is what upsets you. See chapter 5.

impulse.plain: The impulse to act: the inner “go” before you do something.
impulse.why: Other translators write “impulse”. Not motivation in the sense of feeling keen.

office.plain: Public posts and rank. For us: job title, promotion, standing.

slavish.plain: Dependent on someone or something else. A description, not an insult.
slavish.why: Epictetus was born a slave. Free and enslaved are his working terms for the mind, not figures of speech.

great-things.plain: The freedom and calm promised in section 3.

impression.plain: The first picture of an event that lands in your mind, before you have judged it. A disagreeable one is upsetting.
impression.why: You cannot stop impressions arriving. What you do with them is yours.

rules.plain: The tests you have already learned. The first one follows.
rules.why: A _kanōn_ is a builder’s straightedge: you hold it against the thing and look.
